claims.statement: `verify_token` selects its signing key by configuration: when `settings.jwt_secret` is set it verifies with HS256 using that shared secret, and when it is unset it resolves the key per call through `jwt.PyJWKClient(settings.jwt_jwks_url)` and accepts only ES256/RS256.

Every token must satisfy `audience=settings.jwt_audience`, `issuer=settings.jwt_issuer`, required claims `exp`/`sub`/`iat`, a `role` claim equal to `authenticated`, and a `sub` that parses as a UUID; any signature, claim-shape, expiry or UUID failure is collapsed into HTTP 401 "Invalid or expired parent token", which refuses Supabase anon and service-role tokens.

The editor/`hq_role` check is a separate assertion from authentication: with `hq_role` passed, `app_metadata.hq_role` must match it, otherwise HTTP 403 `f"{hq_role.capitalize()} role required"`. Because the claim is read from `app_metadata` (admin-writable) rather than `user_metadata` (user-writable), a parent cannot promote themselves.

Two FastAPI dependencies gate the API: `parent` over `HTTPBearer(auto_error=False)` raises 401 when no credential is present and otherwise returns the verified UUID for all `/v1` parent routes, while the `/v1/editor` router's `editor` dependency additionally passes `hq_role="editor"`; only `/health/live` and `/health/ready` are unauthenticated.

`transaction()` is the single chokepoint turning a caller into database identity: `editor` selects `hq_editor`, `worker=True` selects `hq_worker`, otherwise `hq_api`; it then runs `SET LOCAL ROLE`, `SET LOCAL statement_timeout='10s'`, and `set_config('app.parent_id',...)`/`set_config('app.editor_id',...)` with `is_local=true`, so role and identity cannot leak past the transaction.

`hq.my_parent()` and `hq.my_editor()` convert the transaction-local settings into UUIDs with `NULLIF(current_setting(...,true),'')::uuid`, so an absent identity yields NULL and every policy comparison against it fails closed rather than matching rows.

Household isolation is enforced by RLS policies keyed off `hq.my_parent()`: `own_membership`, `own_household` (membership-based USING, `id=hq.my_parent()` WITH CHECK), `own_child` (household descendants), a `parent_scope` policy on `hq.intakes`/`hq.jobs`/`hq.proposals`/`hq.plans`/`hq.child_goals`, `parent_scope` on `hq.plan_flags` via the owning plan, and `scoped_events` on `hq.events` via its job.

The `own_membership` policy's `WITH CHECK(parent_id=hq.my_parent() AND household_id=hq.my_parent())` is what stops a caller writing itself into another household: under `app.parent_id = parent`, `INSERT INTO hq.memberships VALUES(parent, other)` raises `InsufficientPrivilege`.

Because RLS filters visibility instead of raising errors, out-of-scope rows are indistinguishable from missing ones: another household reading a run, proposal, confirmation or plan receives 404 rather than 403.

`hq_worker` is deliberately outside the parent RLS model for one table only: `worker_queue ON hq.jobs TO hq_worker USING(true) WITH CHECK(true)` lets it claim and update jobs across households; the worker's other transactions supply the claimed job's `parent_id` so the remaining policies still apply.

`hq_editor` is created NOLOGIN with `USAGE` on schema `hq` and no grant on household tables, so an editor reading `hq.children` fails with SQLSTATE 42501 — the editor/parent separation is a role boundary, not a claim check alone.

Editoric catalog writes are constrained by column-level grants rather than RLS: editors get `INSERT`/`UPDATE` only on content columns (title, instruction, age bounds, routine anchor, safety notes, synonyms, world, goal_id) and never on `status`, `reviewed_by`, `reviewed_at`, `withdrawn_at` or `withdrawn_reason`; `created_by` defaults to `hq.my_editor()` so the author is always the caller.

Status transitions, release building/publication and withdrawal are unreachable by direct UPDATE: they are `SECURITY DEFINER` functions with `SET search_path=pg_catalog,hq`, each reading `actor := hq.my_editor()` and raising 42501 'Editor identity required' when NULL, then `REVOKE ALL ... FROM PUBLIC` plus a targeted `GRANT EXECUTE ... TO hq_editor`.

The trust chain continues from `app.editor_id` into those functions: the recorded `hq.catalog_audit` actor and the two-person rules (`Reviewer must differ from author`, `Publisher must differ from release builder`) are all derived from `hq.my_editor()`, so the database enforces them independently of the API.

Service roles never read catalog base tables: `hq_api`/`hq_worker` are granted SELECT only on `hq.current_release`, `hq.published_releases` and the `released_*` views, each of which requires `published_at IS NOT NULL` on the release and `status = 'approved'` on the version.

Editors get a parallel, broader view family granted only to `hq_editor` — `habit_version_details`, `concern_version_details` and the `release_*` views — which filter on neither publication nor approval, so staff can read drafts and unpublished candidates while parents and the worker cannot.

`load_release` switches view families at runtime with `views = "release" if candidate else "released"`, and guards the release id the same way (`hq.catalog_releases` for a candidate, `hq.published_releases` otherwise), so a parent-facing path cannot even name an unpublished release.

Parent writes prefer narrow column grants over broad table grants plus RLS: `UPDATE(resolved_at)` on `hq.plan_flags`, `UPDATE(timezone)` on `hq.households`, and an explicit per-column `UPDATE` list for the profile fields on `hq.children`.

`hq.lock_intake(uuid)` and `hq.lock_release(text[])` are `SECURITY DEFINER` helpers that only acquire locks — the intake one re-asserts `parent_id = hq.my_parent()` and membership, the release one takes `FOR SHARE` on the policy, current release and referenced habit versions — and both are `REVOKE ALL ... FROM PUBLIC` with narrow grants.

`POST /v1/children` writes household, membership, then timezone in that order rather than upserting, because an upsert's new row would have to satisfy the household SELECT policy before the membership row that grants visibility exists.

`LOCAL_DEMO_AUTH` plus `scripts/local_token.py` mint short-lived HS256 development tokens from `JWT_SECRET` (optionally adding `app_metadata.hq_role`), and must stay off on hosted services: `demo_settings()` refuses unless `LOCAL_DEMO_AUTH == "true"` and `JWT_SECRET` is set, and `render.yaml` pins `LOCAL_DEMO_AUTH: "false"`.

Deployment authorization prerequisites: the migrations create `hq_api`, `hq_worker` and `hq_editor` as NOLOGIN roles so the applying database user needs CREATEROLE, and `scripts/setup_db.py` runs `GRANT hq_api,hq_worker,hq_editor TO CURRENT_USER` so the connecting login can `SET LOCAL ROLE` into them.

The `hq` schema is not in `supabase/config.toml`'s exposed `schemas` list (`["public"]`), so the Data API cannot reach these tables and the backend is the only client; a service-role key used as a parent token is refused by the `role == "authenticated"` check.

The RLS boundaries are executed as SQL by the pgTAP suite `supabase/tests/rls.sql`, which switches roles inside one transaction and asserts own-child visibility, hidden foreign children, 42501 for API catalog writes and draft reads, 42501 for an editor reading `hq.children`, and refusal of builder self-publication.

The Python suite exercises the layers above RLS: `tests/test_security_and_changes.py` parametrizes invalid claim sets and a corrupted signature and validates a real RS256 key through a monkeypatched `PyJWKClient`; `tests/test_editorial.py` asserts 401 for no credential, 403 for a parent token and for `hq_role: "support"`, and success for `hq_role: "editor"`; `tests/test_local_scripts.py` asserts locally minted editor tokens verify and parent tokens are refused with 'Editor role required'.

A documented residual authorization gap: release validation runs in the API before `hq.publish_release`, so a direct database caller holding `hq_editor` could publish a release the API would have rejected — the two-person rule and immutability triggers still apply, but the content validation does not.
